text:
Eli: Rolling the new H100 driver (535.86 -> 536.12) across eu-west last night. Canary passed but started seeing sporadic allocation failures when launching inference pods.
Tanvi: saw a few nodes report PTX validation errors in system logs. only on sm90 nodes.
Greg: yep, hit this on a batch job — containers stuck at create time, kube shows CrashLoopBackOff from the nvidia device plugin.
Mira: any NCCL traces? could be RDMA negotiation fallback.
Eli: grabbing logs from node-03 and node-07 now. short dump below:
```
[ 12.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, Ch 00000020, ChID 00000002, 
PTX failure: invalid ptx signature for module "libcudnn.so"
[ 12.346001] nvidia: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel
[ 12.346002] ib_core: failed to create qp: -14
```
Tanvi: that `invalid ptx signature` line is new — we didn't see it on the canary nodes that passed. those nodes have slightly different image build date.
Greg: The device plugin logs show: `failed to init nv_peer_mem: incompatible driver/firmware` and the pod event shows `nvidia.com/gpu: failed to initialize`.
deploy-bot: Rollout paused for driver/536.12 across eu regions — reason: multiple allocation failures detected (threshold 3).
Mira: Quick theory — image builder baked CUDA libs compiled against older PTX and the new driver enforces SM90 PTX signature checks. some nodes still have legacy cudatoolkit packages from image_v2025-11.
Eli: Confirmed: node-03 (/var/lib/image/manifest) shows `cuda-toolkit 12.3.1-build45` vs canary `12.3.1-build48`. small ABI diff but apparently matters with SM90 kernel check.
Tanvi: repro steps I ran: replaced container base image with build45 and it fails on that host, build48 passes. So it's not purely driver -> it's driver+lib mismatch.
Greg: NCCL logs show fallback to TCP on failed IB, which inflates latency and causes some training jobs to time out. For inference fleet it means throughput dips and autoscaler scales up more nodes -> extra spend.
Mira: Immediate mitigation options: 1) roll driver back to 535.86 on affected hosts, 2) update image builder to pin CUDA toolkits to build48 and reprovision nodes, 3) set autoscaler to unschedule new allocations to the affected AZ until images fixed.
Eli: I'm leaning towards (2) + (3). rolling back driver across all eu-west is risky for other services. we can reprovision small subset and redirect traffic.
Tanvi: opened infra ticket INFRA-2042 with logs and node list. adding checklist for image rebuild.
Greg: also adding a quick health-gate in the autoscaler: fail if `/usr/local/cuda/version.txt` doesn't match expected `12.3.1-build48`. that'll prevent new nodes with older toolkit.
ops-bot: Noted. Created incident channel #inc-1719002468 and linked INFRA-2042.
Eli: cost note — during mitigation we expect ~10% capacity loss in eu-west for 4-6 hours while we reprovision. forecasting +$4k/day if autoscaler remains aggressive. cc finance for impact.
Mira: action items: Eli -> coordinate reprovisioning (owner), Tanvi -> update image pipeline and add ptx-signature check in CI, Greg -> add autoscaler health-gate + deploy-bot integration, Mira -> vendor support ticket with cloud GPU partner to check firmware deltas.
Eli: timeline: reprovision 20 nodes by EOD, autoscaler gate in 2 hours, image builder patch in next release.
Tanvi: quick repro command I used: `kubectl run ptx-check --image=redwood/prober:ptx1 --restart=Never --overrides='{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"gpu":"h100-sm90"}}}'` prober output:
```
PTX CHECK v1.2 - host node-03
ptx_validate: FAIL signature_mismatch sm=90 expected=0xabc123 got=0xdef456
```
Greg: added a short smoke test to canary pipeline to run `ptx_validate` against a handful of nodes before driver rollouts.
Mira: temporary workaround: taint affected nodes so scheduler won't place new inference pods. I'll run `kubectl taint nodes node-03 gpu.ptx=bad:NoSchedule`.
Eli: thanks all. keep updates here. I'll update INFRA-2042 with timelines and the rollback plan if reprovision hits blockers.
Mira: moving to monitoring: create dashboard panel for `ptx_validate.failures` and `nvidia.driver.signature_errors` so we catch earlier.
Eli: agreed. closing loop once nodes are reprovisioned.
Greg: follow-up: add a preflight that diffs `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` vs image manifest on boot to catch mismatches before node joins cluster.
Tanvi: noted. I'll start that alongside image fixes.
Mira: thanks team :thumbsup:
